idiom_name: node classes with named attributes (the stdlib ast design)
implementation_notes: The standard library's ast module is this pattern in Python: one class per grammar constructor inheriting a common base, one attribute per named child (BinOp.left, BinOp.right) listed together in _fields for generic tooling, and constructors that accept each field. Hand-written trees follow the same design with plain classes or dataclasses, and node-specific dispatch is written as isinstance chains or, on Python 3.10+, a match statement with class patterns. Keep the class form when nodes carry behaviour; dataclasses add equality and repr when the nodes are pure data.
pitfalls: Attributes are mutable and untyped: node.left = None silently breaks the arity invariant the field name promises unless property setters validate.
Recursive walkers hit the interpreter recursion limit on deep trees, so large inputs need an explicit stack.
dataclass equality recurses through child objects: comparing or hashing two big trees is far more expensive than it looks.
